requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP port 8080 through node1
requirements.summary: Bidirectional TCP/8080 connections through node1 succeed both pre- and post-ACL, and again after all three nodes were independently restarted (data round-tripped in both directions).

requirements.requirement: node1 refuses TCP port 23 passing between node2 and node3
requirements.summary: After the nft reject-with-tcp-reset rule was applied, socat attempts on port 23 in both directions return 'Connection refused', contrasted with success in the pre-ACL baseline. Behavior persists after restart.

requirements.requirement: Rest of the forwarded traffic between node2 and node3 is left untouched
requirements.summary: A control TCP port (9999) and ICMP continue to forward successfully through node1 after the ACL was applied, matching pre-ACL baseline behavior, and ICMP continues to work after all restarts.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (node1, node2, node3)
requirements.summary: For each node, a pre-restart boot_id and healthy state was captured, a reboot was acknowledged, the node became unreachable during reboot, a different post-restart boot_id was observed, and cluster/service state (link IPs, nft ACL, forwarding sysctl, live TCP/ICMP tests) was shown recovered. Boot-id transitions match the fixed global lifecycle snapshots (node1 39fdb9ab->f61cbe93, node2 434803ac->e0ad1783, node3 73237116->ca8f8f03), independently confirming the restarts occurred.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, bidirectional evidence: TCP/8080 forwards through node1, TCP/23 is refused via nft reject-with-tcp-reset, and other traffic (control port 9999, ICMP) is unaffected — all verified before and after a full one-at-a-time restart of node1, node2, and node3, with boot-id changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The main shortfall is operational hygiene: test socat listeners and firewalld port openings created on node2/node3 for validation were not fully torn down and remain active in the final captured state, though they pose low risk and don't affect node1's actual ACL behavior.
limitations: Test artifacts (socat listeners on 8080/23, firewalld runtime port openings) on node2/node3 were left running/open at the end of the trace rather than cleaned up, though they are low-risk and would not survive a future reboot since firewalld changes were not made --permanent.

The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are identical aliases (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor timeline and the after_executor snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were purposeful (link IP assignment, forwarding sysctl, nftables ACL, persistence units) and directly tied to the task or the restart-evidence protocol. However, test infrastructure created for validation was not fully cleaned up: socat TCP-LISTEN processes bound to ports 8080 and 23 on node2 (cmd-79834f66bab54e4a, relaunched after restart in cmd-df4537313d374537) and on node3 (cmd-aaa76d86931c4fa1, relaunched after restart in cmd-7f61c033cf1642d4, cmd-7541ed714bd24b18) were still running and listening in the final after_executor snapshot rather than being torn down, unlike an earlier round of test listeners that the executor did properly kill (cmd-9ad8623f31b24d16, cmd-176eb2c566214c23). Firewalld runtime port openings for 8080/23/9999 on node2/node3 (cmd-fafe7998ef8a4146, cmd-cf996eccaca942d1, cmd-5c863e2ca10948d2, cmd-332e4c5e0cc240b2, cmd-df4537313d374537, cmd-7541ed714bd24b18) also remain open in the final state; these are runtime-only (not --permanent) so they will not survive a future reboot, but they are unrestored residue at task end. These are bounded, low-risk artifacts (test listeners/firewall rules on end hosts, not on node1's actual ACL) rather than destructive or security-weakening changes, but they are leftover residue that should have been reverted after validation.
